title: Standup
text: Standup is async. Post three lines in #kestrel-standup before 10:00 Mountain time: what you finished yesterday, what you are doing today, and anything blocking you. No meeting unless someone is blocked for more than a day.

title: Task board columns
text: TeamPulse has three columns: To do, In progress, Done. A task belongs in In progress only while someone is actively working on it. If you stop working on a task for any reason, move it back to To do and leave a note saying why.

title: Stale tasks
text: A task is stale when it has sat in In progress for seven days or more without an update. Stale tasks are moved back to To do by the stale sweep, with a note, so the board shows what is really being worked on. Moving a task back is not a judgment about the person.

title: Pull request reviews
text: Every pull request needs one approving review before merge. Reviews should be done within one working day. If a review has waited longer than that, the author may ask in #kestrel-dev for a second reviewer.

title: Release checklist
text: Before a release: run the test suite, check the live site in a private window, confirm the rollback commit is known, and post the release note in #kestrel-releases. Releases happen Tuesday through Thursday only, never on a Friday.

title: Rolling back a release
text: To roll back, revert the release commit on main and push. GitHub Pages rebuilds within a few minutes. Post in #kestrel-releases that a rollback happened and why. Do not force-push.

title: On-call
text: One person is on call each week, rotating alphabetically by first name. The on-call person watches #kestrel-alerts and triages anything reported by a teammate within two hours during working hours.

title: Working hours
text: Core hours are 10:00 to 15:00 Mountain time. Outside core hours, nobody is expected to answer messages. Use the schedule-send feature rather than sending late at night.

title: Task notes
text: Each task can carry a short note. Notes are for context the next person needs: a link, a decision, a reason something was paused. Keep conversation in the chat channel, not in task notes.

title: Who can change the board
text: Anyone on the team can add, move, or delete tasks. The stale sweep agent may propose moves but never applies them without a person approving the proposal first.

title: Time off
text: Post planned time off in #kestrel-ooo at least a week ahead and move your In progress tasks back to To do before you leave, with a note about where you got to.

title: Audit log
text: Every agent run is written to the audit log with a run id, a timestamp for each step, and what changed. The log is the first place to look when something on the board seems to have moved on its own.
